historical_smoke_002.diagnostic_limitation: The old transport boundary discarded the SDK exception metadata before the smoke summary was built. The exact status and API error body therefore cannot be reconstructed from SMOKE-002.

findings.old_behavior: After retries, generic SDK/transport exceptions were mapped to PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE with a generic message; only timeout, connection, rate-limit, and context-limit behavior had limited distinction.
findings.consequence: HTTP status, API error fields, request ID, and transport category were unavailable to callers.
findings.repair: Defensive status/class mapping now creates ProviderFailureMetadata and uses precise stable ProviderErrorCode values.

findings.old_behavior: ProviderError carried only its stable code and successful-response metadata; there was no bounded transport/API failure contract.
findings.consequence: Failure consumers could not preserve safe provider diagnostics without retaining the raw SDK exception.
findings.repair: Added strict ProviderFailureMetadata, kept separate from ResponseEnvelopeMetadata, and attached it to ProviderError.

findings.old_behavior: A provider failure turn stored only error.code.value in trace.provider_error.
findings.consequence: The runtime terminal retained PROVIDER_ERROR but lost typed attribution before persistence.
findings.repair: The trace now stores the stable code plus the sanitized ProviderFailureMetadata fields.

findings.old_behavior: The smoke summary and failure artifact could report only PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE and a generic runtime terminal message.
findings.consequence: A future provider failure could not be diagnosed from the immutable smoke evidence.
findings.repair: Whitelisted typed provider diagnostics are copied into the turn trace, failure artifact, and final summary without rewriting historical SMOKE-002.

findings.old_behavior: The diagnostic message helper fell back to str(error), which could include SDK-rendered response/request details.
findings.consequence: An exception string could cross the persistence boundary without being an explicit safe field.
findings.repair: Only an explicit SDK message attribute is accepted; common bearer and sk-* patterns are redacted and bounded to 500 characters.
findings.remaining_risk: SDK-specific message attributes vary; when no explicit safe message exists, message_summary is null rather than reconstructed from exception repr.
